title: Acute Dyspnea: Pulmonary Edema, PE, Asthma and Pneumothorax
subject: Emergency Triage
preview: Acute dyspnea is a symptom; look for immediate threats such as pneumothorax, pulmonary edema, severe asthma and pulmonary embolism.
quickRevision: Acute dyspnea is a symptom; look for immediate threats such as pneumothorax, pulmonary edema, severe asthma and pulmonary embolism.
Wheeze is not specific to asthma, and a quiet chest during severe airflow obstruction may be ominous.
Pulse oximetry, work of breathing, hemodynamics, ECG and targeted imaging direct urgency.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Acute dyspnea is a symptom; look for immediate threats such as pneumothorax, pulmonary edema, severe asthma and pulmonary embolism.
Unilateral reduced breath sounds with shock raises concern for tension pneumothorax; diffuse crackles may favor pulmonary edema.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Wheeze is not specific to asthma, and a quiet chest during severe airflow obstruction may be ominous.
Pulse oximetry, work of breathing, hemodynamics, ECG and targeted imaging direct urgency.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A normal oxygen saturation does not independently exclude pulmonary embolism.

quiz.question: Which bedside finding may suggest tension pneumothorax in a deteriorating patient?
options: Unilateral reduced breath sounds with instability
quiz.explanation: Unilateral reduced breath sounds with instability. Unilateral reduced breath sounds with shock raises concern for tension pneumothorax; diffuse crackles may favor pulmonary edema.
